pages.text: In the $(item)Crystal Growth Furnace$() a seed crystal is dipped into the melt and drawn slowly up, turning - the Czochralski method. The melt freezes onto it as one crystal. Its $(item)Iridium Crucible$() is made of Iron-Nickel: a planet's core, and the iron meteorites, hoard the iridium the crust lacks.

Hold the melt a little above its melting point: the superheat sets how steeply the temperature falls at the growth front, G. Then pull at v so that $(thing)v/G$() sits near 3 - Voronkov's critical ratio: faster and the crystal traps vacancies, slower and it traps interstitials.

An impurity enters the crystal only k_eff as readily as it sits in the melt. Pull slowly and turn fast, and k_eff falls to its lowest: the impurities stay in the crucible. Optical boules must be 99.75-99.85% pure: close to the limit k₀ sets.
Sapphire from corundum (best from a whole $(item)Corundum Crystal Mass$()), fluorite from fluorspar, and garnet from garnet with a rare earth - the dopant that makes garnet a laser crystal.
